lines.trans: Good morning! Why is everyone inside the hallway wall?
Come and see, Carmen! We have found Room Nine!
What lovely windows! May I come in?
Mind the step, madam. Help me fold this sheet.
One, two... oh! Look at that dark, shiny wood!
An upright piano! A real walnut piano!
Careful with the lid: it has been closed for many years.

words.gloss: has been (lleva cerrada = has been closed)

lines.trans: Look at the keys, Clara. They are clean and whole.
Go ahead, Carmen! Play a chord for the house.
Listen... a little low, very warm and... middle D makes no sound!
Every key sounds except one in the middle?
With one good repair, Mateo, an old piano remembers every song.

Every key sounds except one in the middle?
With one good repair, Mateo, an old piano remembers every song.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Several musical notes played together.

examples.trans: She plays a very soft chord.
This chord sounds sad.

meanings.note: Warm invitation to enter a room or proceed.

examples.trans: Come in, the door is open!
Go right ahead, you may sit here.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; ayudar a + infinitive.

examples.trans: Shall I help you with those two boxes?

examples.text: Siempre ayudamos a los nuevos vecinos.
examples.trans: We always help the new neighbours.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.trans: I am thirty years old.

examples.text: Este año vamos a la playa en julio.
examples.trans: This year we're going to the beach in July.

meanings.note: Very common in Spain for things, places and moments: ¡Qué bonito!

examples.trans: What a lovely day!

examples.text: Valencia tiene un centro muy bonito.
examples.trans: Valencia has a very pretty centre.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: El suelo está limpio y brillante.
examples.trans: The floor is clean and shiny.
She has bright eyes.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: The written accent drops in the plural: canciones.

examples.text: Esta canción es de mi abuela.
examples.trans: This song is my grandmother's.
We sing songs in the car.

meanings.note: En casa = at home (without article).

examples.text: Mi casa está cerca del mar.
examples.trans: My house is near the sea.
Today I'm having lunch at home.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; el re central = middle D.

examples.trans: The central station is close.

examples.text: Busco la plaza central del barrio.
examples.trans: I'm looking for the main square of the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: El centro is downtown.

examples.trans: We go to the centre by bus.

examples.text: Pon la mesa en el centro de la sala.
examples.trans: Put the table in the middle of the room.

meanings.note: Adjective from cerrar.

examples.text: La tienda está cerrada los domingos.
examples.trans: The shop is closed on Sundays.

examples.text: Deja la ventana cerrada, hace frío.
examples.trans: Leave the window closed, it's cold.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Con cuidado = carefully; ¡Cuidado con...! = Mind the...!

examples.trans: Watch out for the dog!
Carry the cake carefully.

meanings.note: Describes warm sound, light, or hospitality.

examples.trans: Valencia has a warm climate.
She is a very warm person.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.trans: There are four tables inside.
I will be back in ten minutes.

doblar.gloss: to fold; to double; to turn (a corner)

meanings.en: to fold; to double; to turn (a corner)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: I fold the napkin neatly.

examples.text: Dobla la esquina junto a la farmacia.
examples.trans: Turn the corner beside the pharmacy.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: Today is a good day.
I work eight hours a day.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: encuentro).

examples.text: No encuentro mis gafas de leer.
examples.trans: I cannot find my reading glasses.
We found a terrific bakery.

meanings.note: Sigue entera = it is still in one piece.

examples.trans: He eats the whole pizza.
I work the whole day.

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

meanings.note: Single step of a staircase (plural: escalones).

examples.text: Cuidado con el escalón al entrar.
examples.trans: Mind the step as you go in.

examples.text: El gato duerme en el primer escalón.
examples.trans: The cat sleeps on the first step.

meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'to' before things (escucha el agua).

examples.text: Escucho los pájaros desde mi cama.
examples.trans: I listen to the birds from my bed.

examples.text: Escuchamos la lluvia sobre las tejas.
examples.trans: We listened to the rain on the tiles.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: In music it means a deep, low sound; elsewhere it means serious.

examples.text: Tiene una voz grave y bonita.
examples.trans: He has a deep, lovely voice.
It's nothing serious, don't worry.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.text: Quiero una habitación con vistas al mar.
examples.trans: I'd like a room with a sea view.

examples.text: Mi habitación está en el segundo piso.
examples.trans: My room is on the second floor.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.trans: The room is already clean.
I need a clean towel.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.trans: The table is made of wood.

examples.text: Me gusta el olor de la madera.
examples.trans: I like the smell of wood.

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.
Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: The nut itself is la nuez; de nogal = made of walnut wood.

examples.text: La mesa del comedor es de nogal.
examples.trans: The dining table is made of walnut.

examples.text: Hay un nogal muy viejo en el pueblo.
examples.trans: There is a very old walnut tree in the village.

meanings.note: Las nueve = nine o'clock.

examples.text: El tren llega a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The train arrives at nine on the dot.
We saw a nine out of ten.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.
examples.trans: Oh, sorry, I had not seen you.

meanings.note: Azul oscuro = dark blue; gris oscuro = dark grey.

examples.trans: The hallway is very dark.
I prefer dark chocolate.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la pared, las paredes.

examples.text: Hay un cuadro en la pared.
examples.trans: There is a picture on the wall.
We are painting the walls white.

meanings.note: The corridor inside a house, hotel or train.

examples.text: El baño está al final del pasillo.
examples.trans: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
Don't run in the corridor.

meanings.note: Tocar el piano = to play the piano.

examples.trans: My daughter plays the piano.

examples.text: Hay un piano viejo en el salón.
examples.trans: There's an old piano in the living room.

meanings.note: Un poco de mantequilla = a little butter.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco de miel en el té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little honey in your tea?

examples.text: Quedan pocos minutos para el mediodía.
examples.trans: Few minutes remain until noon.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Also used as an affectionate noun (queridos míos = my dears).

examples.text: Querida Ana: te escribo desde Valencia.
examples.trans: Dear Ana, I'm writing to you from Valencia.

examples.text: Es un lugar muy querido para mí.
examples.trans: It's a place very dear to me.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Spain names notes do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, si instead of letters.

examples.trans: This song starts on D.

examples.text: Do, re, mi: así empiezan las notas.
examples.trans: Do, re, mi: that's how the notes begin.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: recuerdo).

examples.trans: I remember that afternoon perfectly.
Do you remember where we put the blueprint?

meanings.note: From reparar, to repair; plural reparaciones.

examples.text: La reparación del coche es cara.
examples.trans: The car repair is expensive.
The lift is under repair.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam.

examples.text: La señora García vive en el tercero.
examples.trans: Mrs García lives on the third floor.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Sábanas limpias = clean sheets.

examples.trans: I change the sheets on Saturdays.
The white sheet is clean.

meanings.note: Shortened form of tanto used before adjectives and adverbs (¡qué mañana tan luminosa!).

examples.trans: What a peaceful courtyard!

examples.text: ¿Por qué sale el agua tan fría?
examples.trans: Why is the water running so cold?

meanings.note: The lid of a box, pot or piano; in a Spanish bar also a small plate of food.

examples.text: ¿Dónde está la tapa de la olla?
examples.trans: Where is the lid of the pot?
We order a small plate of tortilla.

meanings.note: A door key is la llave; a piano key is la tecla.

examples.text: Esta tecla del ordenador no funciona.
examples.trans: This computer key doesn't work.

examples.text: El piano tiene teclas blancas y negras.
examples.trans: The piano has white and black keys.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

venir.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

meanings.en: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)
meanings.note: Irregular: vengo, vienes, viene, vine.

examples.trans: Thank you for coming this morning.

examples.text: Nos vemos la semana que viene.
examples.trans: See you next week.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.trans: Open the window, it's hot.

examples.text: Mi mesa está al lado de la ventana.
examples.trans: My desk is next to the window.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: Is it true that you're leaving?
I always tell the truth.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; un piano vertical = an upright piano.

examples.text: Escribe la palabra en una línea vertical.
examples.trans: Write the word in a vertical line.

examples.text: Tenemos un piano vertical en casa.
examples.trans: We have an upright piano at home.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: My car is very old.

examples.text: Leo un libro viejo de mi abuelo.
examples.trans: I'm reading an old book of my grandfather's.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.
